input.heading: Source Chapter: Grid-Scale Battery Storage Economics (academic, fictionalized)

output.executive_summary: We assembled a dataset of 142 grid-scale battery installations commissioned between 2015 and 2023 across four regional markets [1]. Installation records were cross-validated against interconnection queue filings and operator disclosure reports (Smith et al., 2021). Each installation was characterized by rated power, energy capacity, cell chemistry, and annual degradation measurements collected over a minimum of three operating years [2].
bullet_points: We assembled a dataset of 142 grid-scale battery installations commissioned between 2015 and 2023 across four regional markets [1].
Installation records were cross-validated against interconnection queue filings and operator disclosure reports (Smith et al., 2021).
Each installation was characterized by rated power, energy capacity, cell chemistry, and annual degradation measurements collected over a minimum of three operating years [2].
The final panel covers 31,400 megawatt-hours of cumulative installed capacity, representing 87% of global deployments in the study window.
Table 1: Annual capacity retention by cell chemistry.
Lithium titanate cells degraded slowest but carried a 2.4 times capital cost premium, consistent with earlier laboratory estimates (Chen and Okafor, 2022).
We computed levelized costs of storage using a discounted cash flow model with a 7% real discount rate and 20-year project life [4].
The model internalizes augmentation purchases that restore capacity as cells degrade, which earlier studies treated as an exogenous sensitivity [5].
Table 2: Levelized cost of storage by market, 2023 USD per megawatt-hour.
output.thorough_summary: We assembled a dataset of 142 grid-scale battery installations commissioned between 2015 and 2023 across four regional markets [1]. Installation records were cross-validated against interconnection queue filings and operator disclosure reports (Smith et al., 2021). Each installation was characterized by rated power, energy capacity, cell chemistry, and annual degradation measurements collected over a minimum of three operating years [2]. The final panel covers 31,400 megawatt-hours of cumulative installed capacity, representing 87% of global deployments in the study window. Lithium titanate cells degraded slowest but carried a 2.4 times capital cost premium, consistent with earlier laboratory estimates (Chen and Okafor, 2022). We computed levelized costs of storage using a discounted cash flow model with a 7% real discount rate and 20-year project life [4]. The model internalizes augmentation purchases that restore capacity as cells degrade, which earlier studies treated as an exogenous sensitivity [5].
